hub-python.summary: Hub-to-hub module forwarding always fails: dev_route builds the forward URL from `path`, which is not a parameter or global of dev_route (symtable confirms global-unassigned), so every hub:<ip>/<dev> call raises NameError and answers 502.
hub-python.reason: def dev_route(self, method, what, q) has no `path` parameter/binding; symtable reports path 'global', assigned=False, and no module-level `path` exists — the NameError at "url = \"http://%s:%d%s?%s\" % (hub_ip, PORT, path, ...)" is caught by the except at 3367 which returns send_err(..., 502).

hub-python.summary: POST /api/report (unauthenticated by design) writes to a filename built from the client-supplied `time` field with only ':' replaced, so '../..' survives and an anonymous poster can write *.json files outside reports/ (toward known_hubs.json, config/, projects, hub_auth.json).
hub-python.reason: "fname = rep_dir / (report["time"].replace(":", "-") + "_" + report["id"] + ".json")" with t = data.get("time") straight from the body, and hub_auth.OPEN lists "/api/report" as ungated — only ':' is sanitized so ../.. escapes reports/; one caveat: the server-appended "_<uuid12>.json" suffix means an attacker picks the directory+prefix but cannot hit one exact existing filename.

hub-python.summary: POST /api/flash/bus replaces a board's firmware via the command channel but is absent from hub_auth.GATED/GATED_POST (exact-string match), so unlike /api/flash, /api/ota and /api/flash/remote it needs no login.
hub-python.reason: "if path == \"/api/flash/bus\" and method == \"POST\": return self.send_json(flasher.start_bus(...))", and gated() is exact-match ("if path in NEVER_GATED ... if path in GATED ... return path in GATED_POST and method == POST") — "/api/flash/bus" appears in none of the lists while "/api/ota", "/api/flash/remote" are in GATED and "/api/flash" in GATED_POST.

hub-python.summary: The never-gated emergency /api/stopall calls modules_here(), which can run (or wait on) a full USB sweep held under _usbscan_lock with a 20 s budget, delaying every board's MOVE STOP by up to ~20 s.
hub-python.reason: "for m in modules_here():" precedes every dev_cmd(r.get("dev"), "MOVE STOP"); probe_usb_all(False) does "with _usbscan_lock:" then "budget = 20" when the cache is older than 8 s, so the stop waits out a full sweep (plus any lock already held by another scan) before the first STOP is sent.

hub-python.summary: Open endpoints read bodies with no ceiling: ungated POST /api/model/upload does write_bytes(self.body()) with limit=0 (reads whatever Content-Length claims into RAM, then to disk), and /api/report reads raw Content-Length unbounded — disk/memory fill from any phone, no login. DRAIN_LIMIT is only applied on refusal paths.
hub-python.reason: "(MODELS / name).write_bytes(self.body())" calls def body(self, limit=0) which does "return self.rfile.read(n) if n else b''" for whatever n Content-Length claims; /api/report likewise does self.rfile.read(length) at 3822; DRAIN_LIMIT appears only inside drain() (refusal path), and NEVER_GATED includes "/api/model/upload".

hub-python.summary: dev_download treats any board reply starting with 'ERR' as EOF, so a mid-file error ends the loop and the partial bytes are served as a complete download with 200 — a corrupted file arrives looking fine.
hub-python.reason: "if r == \"EOF\" or r.startswith(\"ERR\"): break" then "out += chunk" and "return out" — the sole caller at 3465 is "return self.send_bytes(dev_download(dev, ...), \"application/octet-stream\")" with no length or integrity check, so a truncated file ships as a 200 download.

hub-python.summary: ShowPlayer.stop joins the clock thread for 3 s but a @peer command waits up to PEER_WAIT=8 s; on timeout stop() sets thread=None and reports stopped while the old thread is still mid dev_cmd — after a restart clears stop_flag the abandoned thread can keep playing (two clocks, the fault check_takeover exists to prevent).
hub-python.reason: "th.join(timeout=3.0) ... self.thread = None" runs regardless of whether the thread finished, while dev_cmd uses "wait or (PEER_WAIT if peer else None)" with PEER_WAIT = 8.0 — a restart inside the remaining ~5 s window executes "self.stop_flag.clear()" (line 1312), so the old thread's next flag check passes and it keeps sending POSE beside the new clock.

hub-python.summary: The main hub binds with ThreadingHTTPServer's inherited allow_reuse_address=1, which the code's own Polite class (port-80 redirect) explicitly rejects as unsafe on Windows — two MiceHub instances can both hold :PORT and connections land on either unpredictably.
hub-python.reason: main() does "srv = ThreadingHTTPServer((HOST, PORT), Handler)" inheriting allow_reuse_address=1, while class Polite at 4487 sets "allow_reuse_address = False" with the comment that on Windows SO_REUSEADDR "lets one process bind a port another process is already listening on, and then which of them gets a connection is anyone's guess."

hub-python.summary: POST /api/reports (status update) and the background _translate_report_later both do read-modify-write of the same report JSON with no locking; the translator can run up to 180 s, so closing a report while translation is in flight silently loses either the status or text_en.
hub-python.reason: Status update does "j = _json.loads(f.read_text(...)); j[\"status\"] = status; write_atomic(f, ...)" (3914-3917) with no lock, and _translate_report_later does "urlopen(req, timeout=180)" then "data = json.loads(fname.read_text(...)); data[\"text_en\"] = out; write_atomic(fname, ...)" (173-180) — last writer wins whole-file, so whichever field the other wrote is lost.

hub-python.summary: Flasher.start calls _claim but assigns/starts the new thread object outside the lock, so a second POST landing in the claim-to-start gap also passes running() and spawns a second flash job (two esptools on one cable) — the residual gap ShowPlayer closed with its _starting lock.
hub-python.reason: _claim checks "if self.running(): raise" under self.lock but only writes port/type/log fields; "self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self._run, args=(cmd, im), daemon=True); self.thread.start()" sits at 2719-2720 outside any lock, and running() reads self.thread — so a second _claim in that gap sees the stale/None thread; _run's brief "with _flash_lock: _flash_ports.add(port)" does not serialize the esptool subprocess itself.

hub-python.summary: start_received creates a temp dir and decodes the received image BEFORE _claim; if _claim refuses ('already flashing') the folder with the full firmware image is never removed — cleanup lives only in the part-parse except and in _run's finally, neither of which runs.
hub-python.reason: "d = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=\"mice_fw_\"))" at 2746; shutil.rmtree(d) runs only in the part-decode except (2763-2764), and "self._claim(port, module_type, \"usb\")" at 2769 raises "already flashing %s - one board at a time" before the thread starts, so _run's finally rmtree(im["tmp"]) (2857-2859) never executes — the folder leaks.

The same class was fixed for OTA — line 1026 comment 'THE LOGIN IS CHECKED HERE, NOT ONLY IN THE HANDLER ABOVE.'

firmware-core.reason: commands.json:48 has "query": true; WebPortal.cpp:620 `if (COMMAND_DOCS[i].query || COMMAND_DOCS[i].safety) return true;`; GROUP handler (CommandRouter.cpp:115-136) calls id_->setGroup(g), notes 'the AP password changes with the group', and restarts the radio.
